text.en:
Misty's timed adventure now explores like autopilot, and how far she goes depends on her level. Level 1 and 2: her home world, visiting each place's door. Level 3: she also flies into the cell worlds. Level 4: she breaks out and drifts round the spirit world's outer sky. Level 5: she goes inside its bubbles. Level 6: she rides the streams from bubble to bubble on her own. Autopilot (three quick taps on the controller) is a separate choice and always goes everywhere, whatever her level. Her Misty card shows what is unlocked, and the trip sheet says how far this trip reaches.

You can now call Misty back from her exploration whenever you like. While she is out, the timer in her empty bubble says "Tap to call her back": one tap and she flies straight home into her bubble, brings her find with her, and you have her back on the controller. The same button is in the sun panel. Her next trip is tomorrow, and the world keeps the glow she gave it so far.

No more in-between when Misty leaves a world. Out of a cell world, and out of the main world, she goes straight from inside to outside: one moment she is in the world, the next she is outside next to its bubble, while the inside softly fades away. The light streaks, the big glowing disc and ring, the flat colour screen and the purple sheet are gone. The flat blue screen had a real cause: when the camera pulled back, the whole live world was faded out by mistake. That is fixed, so the world now stays on screen.

Holding forward no longer puts a constant light in front of Misty. Instead she pushes against her own stretchy bubble skin, just like when she pushes out of her first bubble: it stretches out ahead of her the way she is flying, a little further as she gets going, and wobbles back when you let go. It tilts with the controller, so you can still see where she is heading, and when you back up it stretches behind her. The energy shot stays exactly as it was (hold the controller and double tap with a second finger), and now it punches out through her skin.

Every panel now opens like Move. Tap Fasting, Meals, the weather, Today or the sound button and the panel grows out of the spot you touched, like a small bubble stretching open, and shrinks back into it when you close it. It floats as one of Misty's see-through bubbles with the world still visible behind it. The quick choices are round bubbles that pop in one after another, like Move's Quick to Epic: the times in End your fast, Snap food and Scan a product, and the weather readings. The main button glows mint like a filled Move bubble. Everything inside still works the same.

Out in the spirit world, holding the controller still (forward) now flies Misty into another world's bubble, just like steering into it with the stick. Before, only the stick counted, so the forward hold bounced off every bubble and slid round it. A steady push now also gets through when the glass nudges her back a little.

Touching the world no longer brings the menus back while Misty flies. On autopilot or while you steer, drag the world round, hold it or pinch it, and the clean view stays: no panels, no menu bar. Only a quick, still tap on Home's own world brings everything back, and that tap does nothing else. Out in the spirit world a tap never brings the panels back: on autopilot it only brings back the controller, so you can take over.

Misty stays busy when she flies out of a world on autopilot. On the way out she looks where she's going instead of turning to stare at you, and once she's out she heads straight for her next stop instead of drifting and waiting. When she gets lost far out, she swims in little loops instead of just hanging there. If you tapped inside a world, leaving it no longer brings up all of Home's menus by surprise. Only the controller you tapped back stays, and one tap on Home brings the rest.

Flying far out no longer drops Misty back in her bubble. If you keep holding one way past the deep dark, she now comes round beside home and keeps flying into new space, instead of straight back into her bubble. Letting go of the stick to turn the view around no longer counts as doing nothing, so she stays out there while you look. A drag from the screen edge while she flies now turns the view instead of switching pages. And switching apps for a moment, or the phone briefly taking the 3D graphics away, now pauses her where she is instead of starting over.

Now the cell guide glows in the dark, not Misty. Deep in a world's dark zone, the little guide flying next to Misty lights up for a split second every 3 seconds, with a soft light that shows just what is right around the two of you. Misty herself stays dark. The faint warm glow of the world you came from is still there, and the dark is still nearly black.

On autopilot, turning the world now shows Misty from a new side. Inside a world, her path stays where it is in the world, so when you drag the world round you see her side, her front or her back from your new angle, and she no longer keeps the same side to you. If your turn carries her goal out of view, she picks a new one in view. And when she has been flying away from you for a while, she now looks back over her shoulder at you for a moment, then flies on. When you steer her yourself, nothing changes.

On autopilot inside a world, the controller now fades out completely, together with its little mode line, so it's just Misty and the world. When you steer her yourself it stays, and one tap still brings it back so you can take over.

Lost in the dark? Look for home. When you fly Misty far out into a world's dark zone, the world you came from now glows very faintly where it really is, in a dim warm light. Even when it is off the edge of the screen, the side facing it is a touch less black. It is only a hint, not an arrow: the dark stays nearly black, the guide still glows every 3 seconds, and finding your way back is still up to you.

Inside a world it's just you, Misty and the world now. The menu, the side bar, the greeting, the weather, the Daily Quest, Today and the buttons no longer show up in there, not even when you tap. Misty, her guide and the controller stay, and the World map button is still there to take you back. Outside the worlds, everything keeps the soft water look from Home instead of the old flat boxes.

The black holes are gone. Nothing pulls Misty in or traps her any more. Where the cloud wall round a world has its dark gaps, the world now opens onto the dark, and you can always fly in there. The deeper you go, the darker everything gets, until you and Misty can hardly see a thing, as if you had flown out of the game. Every 3 seconds her cell guide glows for a split second, so you know you are still there and nothing froze. Steer back and the light comes back. The dark is never a way out. Only the cloud wall is: push into it and its thin glass bubble skin bulges out around her, like Home's edge when she leaves for the spirit world.

Misty no longer stares at you all the time. Out in the world she turns her whole round body to look where she is flying: fly her sideways and you see her face in profile, fly her away and you see her back, fly her up and her face tips to her top. When you steer, she faces the way you turned her, and backing up she keeps facing forward. On autopilot and while she circles a world before going in, she looks along her path. When she rests, she looks around on her own and only now and then glances back at you. Her turns are smooth, never a snap.

Misty now meets the blood cells floating around her. Out in the bloodstream at Home a cell can really bump into her, only when it is truly at her depth, not when it just passes in front of her or behind her. She gets knocked a little, the cell tumbles off into a new lane, and she goes funny and dizzy: she tips over, sways woozily for a moment, braces herself and steadies back up. On autopilot she sometimes spots a cell coming and swerves, sometimes she does not; now and then she drifts over to look at a passing cell. When you steer, she never swerves by herself. After a bump things stay calm for a few seconds, so there is no pinball. No XP, energy or anything else changes.

Beyond your world, every bubble you find can now be visited. Fly Misty against one and keep pushing in for a moment: its skin gives, she slips inside, and the camera comes in close so its glowing walls are all around her. Push against the wall from inside for a moment to get out again. The light strings between those bubbles are ocean currents now: fly close to one and it carries Misty along, fast with the flow, slow and hard work against it; steer sideways to leave it. Autopilot and the way home are never pulled off course, and none of this gives XP.

Home is zoomed out now. When you open the app, the camera starts close to Misty and gently pulls back, so you see more of her world with Misty in the middle. Her four bubbles, Meals, Move, Water and Fasting, slowly circle around her like Dragon Balls. They stop the moment you touch one, so tapping and long pressing work exactly as before. Pinch in any time to come close again. With your phone on its side they stay in their usual spots.

Ways out: inside a world, the soft cloud wall at its edge, in Misty's own blue, violet and cyan, is the way out. Fly her into it and keep pushing for 3 seconds: the wall stretches where she presses, Home's light shows through behind it, then it bursts open and you both fly out. The autopilot heads for the cloud wall, and World map always brings you home. Misty's guide and hints stay quiet while she travels between worlds.

Misty's controller now stays put. Out in the world, while you steer, on autopilot or inside a world, it keeps its spot on the screen instead of moving around with Misty or the camera, so your thumb always finds it in the same place. It only moves when you turn your phone or iPad, and then it stays put again. Everything you do with it works the same.

Energy shot: while one finger holds Misty's controller, dragging or held still in the middle, tap the world twice quickly with another finger (or tap Misty twice). She shoots a ball of energy the way she is aiming: straight ahead, or up and down with the controller. Where it lands inside a world, the world heals a little and its murk and fog thin. It needs a moment to charge between shots, and each world can only be healed so much a day, so it can't be farmed. It never gives XP or crumbs. Without a finger on the controller, a double tap works exactly as before.

Meals is one simple thing now. Tap the Meals bubble and the Log a meal sheet opens with everything in it. Long press it to see today's meals, and letting go after the long press no longer opens a second sheet. The bubble holds its spot instead of creeping around. The Daily Quest no longer asks you to log a meal right next to the Meals bubble: it suggests your other quests first, its meal button opens the same Meals sheet, and a meal you log in the bubble counts for the quest too, once. Past the edges that give way there are no walls any more. New worlds keep appearing the farther you fly, and you can fly right into them. Let go for a while and Misty always finds her way home.

Smoother bubbles: the outlines of Misty's bubble, every Home bubble (Fasting, Water, Move, Meals, VR, Sound, World map, Day/Night, Today, the weather and the Daily Quest) and the other worlds out in the universe are smooth now instead of jagged and pixely, also when your phone is warm or in Low Power Mode. The wide Daily Quest and Today drops have rounder corners too. It costs no extra battery: the bubbles stay as alive as before, only their edges are cleaner. The menu bar stays as it was. The little cell guide stays with Misty now. When the menus fade while she flies, on autopilot or while you steer, the guide and its speech bubble stay beside her instead of vanishing. Its bubble has a real tail that touches the guide, also when the guide is the small helper next to Misty, and it never sits on the Daily Quest or the crumb line under it, even while those are faded, on a phone held upright or sideways and on iPad. One tap still brings all the menus back.

The menu now stays hidden while you fly: when Misty leaves a world, floats home or stops, the menu and buttons no longer pop back by themselves a second later. Tap anywhere once to bring them back.

Small maintenance update, no new gameplay in this one. It is a fresh build so you can check that your phone picks up updates right away. Nothing in the app changed. The next updates with real changes are being built now.

Fly Misty anywhere: inside a world, touch Misty herself and drag left or right to turn her. Only she turns, the world stays put, and a few soft lights in front of her show which way she faces. Touching anywhere else still turns the world. Hold her controller still in the middle and she flies straight ahead into the world, and the camera swings in behind her. Tap twice and she backs up for a moment, then stops by herself. Tap once, then hold, and she keeps backing up. While you hold, slide the controller left or right to steer and up or down to climb or dive. Three quick taps start the autopilot (that used to be a double-tap). She can now fly much further, right out to the edges and down into the dark of each world, so you can get a little lost and find your way back. Fixed: tapping Meals (and every other sheet that slides up from the bottom) opens properly again. Since the level bubble update those sheets were opening invisible. The Meals bubble also stays in its spot while Misty flies, and the 3D bubbles no longer turn pixely when your phone gets warm or is in Low Power Mode.

Some edges give way if you push long enough.

Home is symmetric now. Four living bubbles sit around Misty: Meals and Move on top, Fasting and Water below. The new one, upper left, is Meals: it shows how many meals you've logged today, like 2/3, and fills up as you go, because every meal charges Misty. Tap it to log a meal, or long press it to see today's meals. The sun/moon button moved down to sit above Sound, the same way VR sits above World map, and it still works the same. The weather is a round bubble now, with its icon above the temperature. The Daily Quest and the Today pill are real liquid drops now, curved all the way round with no straight lines. Mist rule: inside a world, the mist and clouds around its edge are the forbidden edge. Push Misty into them and she can wander out there and get a little lost: she fades into the mist, can't quite hold a line, and drifts back once you let go. Every world has two clear gaps in the mist where the universe shows through, marked by a soft starlight glow. Only pushing outward through a clear gap for 3 seconds flies you both out. On autopilot she heads for the nearest gap by herself. Day & night menu: tap the sun/moon button three times quickly to open it, and tap anywhere else to close it. It now opens every time. One tap still switches Day and Night. There is no long press any more, and holding your finger anywhere in the app no longer selects text or pops up the copy menu.

Clean flight view: when Misty flies on autopilot, the menu bar, the top row, the bubbles, the Daily Quest and the buttons fade away, so only Misty and her world are left. When you steer her yourself, everything fades except the controller. Tap anywhere once to bring it all back: that tap does nothing else, and she keeps flying. The movement bubble now stays in its own spot while she flies, instead of sliding to where she used to sit.

Misty's ways in and out of worlds now feel like real travel. On autopilot she no longer flies straight in: she circles the world, getting smaller and smaller as she falls closer, like a ship in orbit. The first time she reaches it she skims the edge and gets flung back out, on a low-energy day maybe twice, but she always gets in by the third try. And she can leave a world for real now: steer her against the edge of the world and keep pushing outward for 3 seconds. Light gathers where she presses, and then you both fly out, the camera with her, back into the universe beside the world you left. No more snapping back into her bubble. On autopilot she does the same: she flies to a corner, presses against it for 3 seconds and flies out on her own. Everything that pops up now looks like Misty: reminders like "Your 16 h fast ends at", Misty's gift of the day (it used to say Kometa's), the little praise lines, XP banners, the update bar and the Fast done card all wear her bubble: see-through blue glass with her violet rim, a cyan edge of light and her soft glint. Everything works and sits where it did. Tips now wait for you: a tip only counts as read when you tap it (Nice, OK or its button). If it fades away on its own or you tap past it, it comes back later, and no tips pop up while Misty is flying, on autopilot or while you steer. A journey fact joins your cell's list only when you tap Into the collection. Misty's praise speaks as a cell now, no more leaves or roots. World hunt: the little cell guide next to Misty now talks to you in real speech bubbles, with a tail pointing back at it, instead of pop-ups at the top. Its bubble never sits on the Daily Quest, the crumb line under it or the controls. It says a lot more now: how many crumbs it senses, Warmer! when one is close, which way to try when you're lost, that one is hiding behind you, that crumbs only count when you steer yourself, and three new facts about every world. When Misty cheers, her line comes out of Misty herself. The crumbs are only a game and don't change anything in your real body. Levelling up is quieter now. The big XP card under the Daily Quest is a small bubble of Misty's glass: a thin ring shows how far she is to her next form, with one short line like Next: Glimmer · 70 XP to go. It only shows up when she evolves or gets another quarter of the way, and it's gone after 3 seconds. The level-up note above the menu bar is the same small bubble now, not a gold bar. Tap either one to open your path, as before. Home: VR, Sound, World map, the day/night button, the Today pill, the weather pill and the Daily Quest are now made of Misty's own living bubble, the same one as fasting and water. They shimmer, glow and breathe with her, keep their shape (Today and weather stay pills) and stay exactly where they were. Everything works the same. World hunt: inside a world you can now always see how many are left. A slim line under the Daily Quest shows the world, one dot per crumb and, for example, 2/6 collected · 4 left. When you've caught them all it says World clean, so you know you can fly on. It's a game, not a health reading. Today: a new movement bubble sits next to water and fasting, made of the same living glass. Tap it and four small bubbles bloom out: Quick, Medium, Long and Epic. Pick how your walk or bike ride felt, no minutes or steps to type. The bubble fills up, Misty does a happy dance and you see exactly what it added to her energy. Four quarters fill the day. Only time on your feet or on a bike counts, not sitting on a bus or train. Picked the wrong one? Pick again within a minute and it replaces it. Long press the bubble to see today's moves and remove one again. If you already logged a workout on Move, the bubble is already full, so nothing counts twice. The menu bar, the weather pill and the sun/moon button are now made of the same liquid glass as Misty's bubble: see-through blue glass with her violet rim and a cyan edge of light. Everything is where it was and works the same: same buttons, same weather, same day and night switch. Today: the fasting and water bubbles are now the same living bubble as Misty's, the same glassy shimmer, glow and breathing, and they react to your touch the same way: press and they squish and spring back. Everything they show, like your fasting time, goal and end time or your glasses of water, now sits inside the bubble, just like Misty sits inside hers. The separate Edit button above the fasting bubble is gone: long press the fasting bubble to change when your fast started. Tapping works as before. Misty stays Misty inside every world: when she flies into a world, on autopilot or when you steer her, you now see her there with her energy ring, and the camera follows her. The little cell creature of that world is only her small helper flying beside her. Today's status line now matches her energy ring too. Misty's world hunt: every world now hides little sugar crumbs and murky germs, tucked far away in its corners, 4 on a calm day and up to 10 after spiky meals. Steer Misty with her controller and fly her right up to one: she gobbles it up, gets power and her world clears a little. Clear them all and the world sparkles again. Each one gives power that levels Misty up, makes her a little faster and gives her energy a small boost, up to a daily limit, and each crumb only counts once a day. Flying into a world yourself powers her up too, once per world a day. On a low-energy day the pull is weak and she may bounce off the edge once or twice, so keep trying. The little explainer in each place now flies next to Misty like a sidekick. Inside a place you can pinch to fly much closer, toward the spot under your fingers, and pinch out to float back. It's a game, not a health reading. Misty's energy scale: now you can see exactly how she's doing. A thin ring on her bubble fills with her energy, the two marks on it are the next levels, and her name tag shows the percent. Hold Misty to open her card: her scale from Low to Okay to Full, how far it is to the next level, and the 1 to 3 quickest things that get her there right now, like 1 Move and 2 glasses of water, each with what it adds. It counts with the same fair rules as the world weather, so what it promises really happens, and repeats or fast taps never count. Power-ups from her world hunt show on it too. It's a game world, not a health reading. Today is clean again: there is no extra Adventure button. Misty's adventures start from her controller, just tap it three times. World weather is fast and fair now: your world turns stormy the moment a spiky meal or product is logged, and every good step clears it right away, a little for a glass of water, more for a Move or a low-spike meal. Your last few days only set a gentle starting mood. Logging the same thing twice or tapping fast adds nothing extra. It's a game world, not a health reading. Today: Misty goes on adventures. Tap her controller three times (autopilot) and she drifts slowly through her world like a fish in an aquarium, from corner to corner, sometimes wandering off and getting a little lost before she finds her way back. Gravity pulls her into a world, she shrinks and falls in, and rises out the same way. Touch the controller to steer her yourself, or tap her empty cell and she flies straight home. She brings back small finds, up to 5 a day, and only explores while you watch. Her hints now follow how your world is doing: a stormy sky, a Move calming it, a hazy inside or clear skies, always kindly and only about the game world. When her energy is too low for trips, she tells you what would fill her up again. Move: Mirror mode. Tap Mirror mode on the Move screen, pick Desk chair, Standing at the desk or Floor stretch, put your phone where the guide shows and turn on the camera. You see yourself with a glowing glass outline over you: step into it, hold still, 3-2-1, then move with it. If you leave the picture, it waits for you. Your camera picture stays on your phone, nothing is recorded or sent. No camera? Follow the same outline without it. Move: the workout figure is now a person. Instead of Misty with arms and legs, a human silhouette in the same liquid glass does every exercise with you, in time with the clock, and the muscles you are working glow. Misty stays as she is everywhere else. Faster and cooler: the app does much less work in the background now, so it should feel quicker and keep your phone cooler. The old rain and leaves no longer flash for a split second when you open it. Community: energy balls are now live for everyone. When you shoot with the energy joystick, everyone in the Community sees your ball fly from your companion at the same moment, and you see theirs. It hits the same person on every phone. Scanning is simple now: you see the product, one big answer (will it likely spike your insulin or not, an estimate) and one button, Catch it. Catching earns XP whether it spikes or not, and adds it to the spike lists everyone can browse and search, including foods that look healthy but spike. The estimate is smarter: vegetables, oats and plain dairy no longer show as spikes. Under it: cheaper at other stores, and community deals you can post with the store, price and how long the offer runs. Community: voice notes. Tap the mic next to the message box to record and the arrow to send, or hold the mic, let go to send and slide left to cancel. Tap a play button to listen, in the chat or right in the speech bubble. Photos now show a small picture in the speech bubble. Tap someone's companion to send a stream of light to them and start talking; press and hold a companion to open their person card. Scan has a new look: Snap food opens a full-screen camera with a big shutter, Photos, Type it and a Barcode switch that really jumps to the barcode camera. Your photo, Log a meal, the barcode result and the not-found card are now blue glass on black space, and if the camera is off, a glass card shows you how to turn it on or lets you choose a photo instead. Cook: every meal now has two clear buttons, Cook it and Shop it. They sit on Cook under the shuffle button, on the shuffled meal and on every recipe. Shop it opens your cart in the same blue glass: the stores sit in one row and say which is cheapest, the cart is a glass bubble, and you tick items off right in the list. Shop at … opens a big tick list for exactly those items in aisle order, and the round X no longer covers it. New for grocery shopping: scan a product and see straight away whether it's likely to spike your insulin (spike, mild or no spike, an estimate from the label). One tap on Add to cart puts it on your shopping list as in your cart, and the camera is ready for the next product. Sugar, carbs, fibre, protein and ingredients are under Details if you want them. Turn on Shopping at the top of Scan, or tap Scan a product in your shopping list. New: everyone now gets their own unique companion. During sign-up, your birthday (and your birth time, if you know it) brings a being of light to life. Its star sign gives it a colour and a mythic feature, and the day and hour shape its look, name and personality, so no two companions are alike. It is not a he or a she, it is an entity. Already have an account? Open Profile and tap your companion card to bring yours to life. Today: Misty now goes into the worlds by herself. Open any place and she follows you in a moment later and roams around freely. On autopilot she visits each place on her own, roams inside, then moves on to the next. Today: Ride along and its video screen are gone. Misty already flies your real world. Your inside stays as one short line, tap it to read it all. Body journeys now say what comes next: tap Start next journey and Misty sets off and flies around her galaxy, or see Next journey tomorrow with the time left. The journey log names the place your cell discovered instead of a cut-off sentence. The sun starts fresh every night at midnight, and when it is full it shows when the new sun comes. Fixed: Misty's energy bar stays inside its card. The Today sheet has a new look: dark space with the same blue glass as the weather pill and Daily Quest. Every row and shortcut has the same height and rounded corners, the old mint, beige and orange buttons and bars are now blue glass, the text is easier to read, and the X under it is glass too. Everything works the same. New in Move: Misty now has little glass arms and legs and does every exercise with you in the workout player, marching, curling, walking, bridging, with the working parts glowing. Community: the typing bar is now solid dark blue glass, so you can always read what you write. Speech bubbles behind it fade out while you type. Sound: the string pad on Today now really sets the background sound. The string you touch picks the key, higher is brighter and fuller, and sliding along a string shifts the pitch. You hear it change right away, it stays that way, even after you close the app, and Reset sound brings back the original sound. Fixed: every person card in Community now shows a real join date, also for older accounts. New in Community: an energy joystick in the bottom right corner. Pull it and your companion turns into a pointed energy shape, let go and an energy burst flies. Hit someone and their companion rolls off like a billiard ball, bumping the others, and they get your energy. Then everyone drifts back to their spot. Community: the people now stand out. The world behind them steps back, a little darker and softer, and every companion sits on a bright blue glass disc with a clear name. Community: the worlds start circling each other the moment you open it, no more waiting a few seconds for the background to move. Community: zoomed out, the clear tube that cut a line through the bubbles is gone. Your world now carries soft waves of light instead. iPad: your profile picture and the Day/Night button now sit right next to the weather, in one row under your greeting. New: after every update, "Show me" walks you through each new thing, one by one, like the first tour. Sound: once you turn it on, the calm sound keeps playing in Community, Cook and Move too. It only steps aside while a video, a voice note or the workout plays, then comes back. Scan: typing a barcode number works again. The box and its Go button now sit right above the keyboard, and the water button is gone from the scanner. Your XP card is now blue glass, sits right under the Daily Quest instead of over the top row, and uses Misty's comet forms. Scan: tap Scan and only your iPhone asks for the camera, once. Our own "Allow camera" card is gone. Scan now sits in the same living spirit world as Community, Cook and Move, and the camera fades in over it. If the camera is off, a small blue glass card says so, with a blue Try again button and an easy way to type the barcode number instead. The Scan tab now lights up while you scan. New in Community: the world around everyone is now a living cellular galaxy, with glass cells full of tiny cells and glowing webs, soft curving threads of light and sparkling dust. No more stray companions in the background, so the real people in Community stand out. Fixed in Cook: tapping Post in For You opens the New post window and it stays open, so you can add a link, video, photo or caption and post. For You now opens as a blue glass window inside Cook, in the same spot as Shuffle and Swipe, and you swipe up and down through the posts right there. New on Move: start a workout and it opens full screen over the living world in blue glass. Misty does each move with you, and the body parts doing the work glow. New: the sun/moon button on Today and the video Close and Open buttons in For You now wear the same blue glass as the weather pill. Fixed: double-tap the world on Today to zoom again. It switches between Misty close up and the World map, the same as a tap on the stick. On iPad the check-in reminder now shows as a blue glass card under the top of the page, not up in the status bar. Fixed: person cards in Community show the date someone joined instead of a long number. New in Community: send a photo. Tap the photo button next to the message box, pick one or take one, add a caption if you like and send. It is shrunk on your phone first and its location data is removed. Tap someone's companion to open their glass person card: their picture, star sign and personality only if they chose to share them, when they last wrote, and buttons to chat or send energy. The last old gold and purple buttons, cards and sheets around the app are now the same blue glass as Daily Quest. New: steer Misty out of her bubble. Drag the glass controller and she pushes against her bubble, stretching it like a soap film, then slips out without popping it, at the same size as in her bubble. Fly her anywhere in your world. Near a glowing place she gets smaller, and right at its edge she warps in, the same as tapping it. Inside, she is there with you and you keep steering her. Tap a place instead and you go in without her, as before. Sound is calmer: the world now plays soft pads and singing bowls, and the Move and session timers ring a gentle bowl instead of a beep. Open Sound on Home for a glowing string pad: touch or swipe to play, higher is louder, slide to bend the note. Inside Gut, Pancreas, Brain and the other places, a small glass guide now travels with you and tells you about the place in a Misty-blue bubble. Tap it for the next line. New: on Today, the fasting and water bubbles now look and move like Misty's own bubble: almost clear inside, a soft violet and cyan rim, and the same slow wobble and breathing. New: Cook, Move and Scan now live in the same living spirit world as Community. Leave Today for any of them and the camera pulls out past your bubble; come back to Today and it flies down to Misty again. Fixed: when you travel into a place in your world, its "You arrived" card now sits right under the Daily Quest box, no longer over the sun/moon button and your profile picture. It fades away as soon as you leave the place, go back to Misty, open the World map or switch tabs. New: Community is now your living world, not a picture. Pinch out on Today, or push the World map stick up, and you keep flying out past the World map, out of your own bubble, until you see everyone's glowing bubbles joined by threads of light, with the companions gathered out there. Tap Community and it is the same pull-out as a quick warp; going back flies you down to Misty. A plain tap on the stick switches between the World map and Misty. Move: the workout length buttons (5 to 60 minutes) now sit in one clean, centred glass row under Start and never cover it. Cook, For You: shared YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and Vimeo videos now play right in the feed, in the platform's own player; only links that can't be embedded still open outside. New on iPad: Today has one centre line. Your greeting is at the top, the weather pill sits right under it in the blue glass, and the Daily Quest box is centred below, also with the iPad held sideways. New on Today: the top row is even. The weather pill sits on the left in the same blue glass as Daily Quest, the sun/moon and your picture on the right, your greeting in the middle, and the Daily Quest box is centred right under it, also on iPad held sideways. The weather view is the same see-through blue glass. New: when Misty levels up, you now see her real self in a blue glass card over her world, with her new stage name. New: a little glass controller sits above Today. Drag it and you fly Misty around her world yourself. Tap it three times and she goes on her own adventure that you can just watch, slow and sleepy when her energy is low. Touch it again to take over. The ring around it is her energy. Tap her empty bubble to call her home. Fixed on iPad: in Cook, Swipe now sits next to the tiles instead of below the screen. For You shows Misty's living world around the videos instead of black. The menu bar is the same blue glass as Daily Quest. Coming back from Community no longer flashes old meal and fasting steps. Community is a real map now: everyone keeps their own spot like a pin, so tapping someone selects exactly them and nobody moves. Drag to look around, pinch or double-tap to zoom. Typing keeps the map still and only lifts the message box. Bubbles step aside so they never cover anyone, and the Chat room now shows the companions' replies too. Easier to read: the small grey lines on the Today pill, the Today shortcuts and the Cook and Profile tiles, and the Community chat's small text and send arrow, are now clearly readable. Removed: the microbe buddies and the microbe collection are gone, along with the XP they gave. Misty is your only companion. Fixed: going back to Today from Move, Cook or Scan now glides like iPhone home screens: the world stays put behind both pages, no dark page, no edge, no ghost of the last page. Fixed: World map inside a place now flies you back out with the same warp, played backwards, and lands on the whole world. No more jump. New: tap Misty and she answers: hey, a giggle when you tickle her, slow down if you keep poking, and lines that follow her energy. A World speed slider sits under the day-night slider. The wardrobe is see-through. On iPad, Sound, World map, VR and Kometa's gift line up evenly. New: Community bubbles work like Snapchat's map: each companion's name and newest words sit in a small glass bubble right above them, yours above you. Photos say New picture and open when tapped. The Chat button opens the full group chat. New: Community is now Misty's own world, zoomed out: the camera pulls back from Misty and the companions appear in the same bloodstream. Cook, Move and Profile show the same live world behind them. New: the day-night slider now changes the world gradually, like a real day: morning mist, sun, golden hour, blue mist, night, with no sudden jump. Each world opens zoomed out, double-tap to zoom. Tap Misty to pet her, hold her for her levels. Trip notes now sit inside the Daily Quest box. Fixed: Home → Community no longer flies a rectangle at you. It now moves like a trip to a glowing place: the camera pulls out of Misty's world with the light streaks and the galaxy fades in, and coming back the camera dives into Misty. Fixed: the little freeze every few seconds in Community is gone. Fixed: after coming back from Community you can tap the glowing places on Home again straight away. Community looks like Misty's spirit world from far out, with round cartoon speech bubbles next to whoever is talking. Home → Community now warps out like the trips to places on Home, and a swipe pulls it with your finger. All tabs slide sideways, the camera too. New look for Scan: the camera now matches the rest of the app, with Misty's blue viewfinder, glass buttons and the same dock at the bottom. Tap any tab to leave the camera. New: Misty doesn't smile all the time anymore. Full of energy she looks calm and content, okay she looks neutral, low she looks sleepy or a little sad. When she heads out full of energy, the glowing cells in her world get brighter over her trip and stay that way for the rest of the day. New: Misty's face now follows her energy: she smiles when she's full of energy, looks neutral when she's okay, and sleepy or a little sad when she's low. Her energy comes from the meals, water and Moves you track. Too tired, she stays home; while she's out, her bubble shows when she's back. Spiky meals are still logged but earn no XP, and never cost any. Home and Community still zoom into each other; the other tabs slide. Tabs now slide like iPhone pages: swipe left or right, or tap a tab. Community is now a solar system: you are the sun, every companion is a little world on its orbit. New look: every tab now uses the same dark Liquid Glass design, like iOS. Fixed: on a stormy day the world no longer turns brown, it stays dark blue. New: coming back from the galaxy, the camera now flies back down into Misty instead of Home just growing back into place. Fixed: the small Edit above the fasting bubble on Home can be tapped again. New: when Misty goes on an adventure you now see her flying around the world, stopping to help things grow with rings of light and sparkles. No more 'In the garden' label. When you're tracking well she's bright and quick. When the day's going badly she looks tired and her bubble turns reddish. New look: every bubble on Home now matches Misty's blue glass bubble, including fasting, water, VR, World map, Sound, Today, the Daily quest panel and the menu bar. The fasting bubble shows a small Edit just above it, and the stage hours no longer run into the fasting time. New look: the world is now silvery dark blue instead of red. Day mode is a lighter blue, not white. Fixed: hold the moon/sun button (top right) for half a second to open the Day & night slider again. Sliding it lights the world too. Fixed: on Home, the Today shortcuts (Check-ins, Meals, Your plate, Medicine, Shopping, Extras) no longer float over the world as loose words. They now sit as a row inside Today. New: Community now lives just outside Home. Keep pinching out past Home's widest view and you land in the galaxy with everyone else; spread two fingers on the galaxy to dive back into Home. The Community tab plays the same short zoom, without the blank screen or the giant You, and no arrival card pops up over the galaxy. New: chat bubbles in the galaxy are minimal. No more "You → name" labels: your messages are in your colour, theirs are in their colour, and a message to the whole room is just a bubble next to whoever wrote it. New: Cook reads eBook, Recipes, Products, and For You sits in the middle of the Shuffle | For You | Swipe switch. In Move, the Leaderboard is a card right under the title, and the Safety button is gone (the safety notes are a small line at the bottom). On Home, Misty now gives you the tips in her own speech bubble, and the Daily quest card, Today, VR, World map and Sound all share Misty's clear glass bubble. New: Home to Community is one camera now. Tap Community and you pull straight out of Misty's bloodstream into the galaxy, where Misty becomes your own glowing body. The galaxy is full of individual companions with their own names, ages, levels and forms (they are bots, their profile says so, and chats with them stay on your phone). Talking is clearer: only one line at a time, from you to the person you picked, with the newest message sitting on the middle of that line and an arrow showing who is talking to whom. Tap someone new and the old line is gone; tap You to stop talking. On Home, Edit sits right above the word Fasting, the water and fasting bubbles moved further from Misty, and pressing and holding the water bubble resets today's water to 0. Chat privacy & quiet hours now live in Profile, under Community. New: For You now lives in Cook (tap For You top right) and the Leaderboard lives in Move (tap Leaderboard top right). Community is just the spirit galaxy now: no tabs, no big title, no Privacy & quiet button. New: Home and the places in your body are one world. Tap a glowing place and you travel there right on Home, then World map flies you back. And VR is right on Home: tap VR above World map and tilt your phone to look around. New: Community is now the spirit galaxy. Zoom out from your body and see everyone's bodies floating, with speech bubbles. Tap someone to talk to them directly. New: Home is your body world now. No extra tap to get in: drag to look around, pinch with two fingers to zoom, tap World map to see the whole world and tap a glowing place to travel there. Misty sits in one simple bubble, and the sound button is right on Home. Today opens instantly: no more glimpse of the old Home when you tap back. New: tap Misty and you now see the same Misty as on Home, with her evolution path: her current form big, the XP to her next form and all six forms ahead. Tidied up: dressing up Misty is gone. The wardrobe, outfits, Misty's room with the window and plasma cushion, the shop and the old herb pieces like the Maple crown, Mist scarf and Acorn pot are out. Misty now changes only through her six forms. Your XP and level stay exactly as they are, and nothing of it ever cost you anything. Kometa's gift is now one small glowing spot bottom left in your world, once a day. New in Community: the planet. Your companions stand together on a little planet and talk in speech bubbles. Fixed: Scan. The white Back bar is gone; close the scanner with the round X top left, like every other screen. Deep analyze at the bottom is fully visible again, nothing covers it anymore. The camera now opens every time you open Scan, and starts again by itself when you come back to the app. New in setup: “I want” now lists only real goals like Fewer cravings or More energy. PCOS, insulin resistance and pre-diabetes have their own optional spot, “Anything we should look out for?”, in Profile too. Whatever you tap now lights up green. And the question now asks: When are your cravings strongest? New: Spirit square. Community → Chat is now one shared room with real people, no demo messages. Your type and star sign only show if you choose to share them. Reply, mention and react, drafts are kept, and quiet hours (10 PM to 8 AM, adjustable) keep chat alerts silent at night. Fix: on the iPad held upright, the top bar and quest card no longer sit across Misty in the middle of Home; they are back at the top and you can tap Misty again. New: Home opens into your body world, with Misty at the centre. Water and fasting stay close; tap Today for your log and goals, Misty for her companion sheet, or the zoom button for the whole world. Close sheets with the round X. New: the body world now shows how your day is going. Clear world: bright look and a light, airy sound with soft high tones. When you log spiky food today or scan in spiky products, the world turns stormy: darker, murkier colours and a low rumble joins the sound. A logged Move calms it, and a day without spikes stays clear. The line under the world title says why. It is a game mood, not a health check. New: Misty evolves with you. Her form grows over six stages from your star sign and style, with markings from form 3 and a crown at form 6. She cheers when you log or scan a low-spike meal and braces at sugar bombs (no points for reactions). The longer your fast, the calmer she glows. In her world, tap Evolution (or Wardrobe), then Your companion’s forms to see all six and pick her style. Friends see her form in their friends tree only if you turn sharing on. New: body sound. In the 3D world, tap Sound at the top to turn on light, airy sounds and warp sounds when you fly into a place. It only plays when you turn it on, with its own volume and an off switch. And the autumn leaves stay outside now: no more leaves inside your body. Fixed: the Update button. Tapping Update now loads the new version right away and says it is working. If it takes too long, you can tap Try again, and if it still hangs, close LOWiSPIKE completely and open it again. Offline it tells you to wait until you are back online. New: points only for things you really do. Taps, switching tabs and opening menus give no XP anymore. You earn XP for logging meals and water, finishing a Move session, finishing or correcting a fast, finishing a body journey, a new buddy, care for a friend and the first time you discover a body region. Healthy actions in a row still build a streak: 3 in a row +10, 5 +20, 8 +40 with a big celebration. New: you can fix when your fast started. On Home, tap Edit start on the rim of the water bubble (or in the fasting sheet next to "since"), pick the date and time of your last meal and save. Your fast keeps running; the fast's own points still come once, when you end it. New: arrival cards. When your cell arrives somewhere in your body (a place in the 3D world, the end of a cell ride or a body journey), a gold card shows the place, one real fact about it and how today's entries show up there. Close it with the X; the 3D view stays free to drag. New: Day & night. In Profile > Look & sound, slide through the whole day like a timelapse: morning mist, day, golden hour, blue mist and night stars. Everything in between is there too, and the sky, mist, stars, your cell and the 3D world move with your finger. Jump straight to Day, Night or Auto (follows the real sun). The button top right switches Day and Night with one tap. New: opening the app is clean now. You see one calm LOWiSPIKE screen for a moment, then your finished app appears in one go, no more older screens flashing by first. It also starts faster. New: flying to a place in your body world is one smooth zoom again. Tap a glowing place in the 3D world, or pick it on the World map, and you glide through the bloodstream straight toward it, faster and faster, dive into its glow and land inside. Back pulls you out the same way. The extra row of place buttons at the bottom is gone: the World map (lungs included) and tapping the world are all you need. New: microbe buddies. Lacto moves into your cell as your first buddy, and up to three microbes from your collection can join. They float around your cell, sit with you at home and orbit in the 3D world. They light up at their favourite thing (low-spike food, water, movement …), grow closer every day, and one comes along on your body trips. Tip: tap a buddy in your herb. New: your world follows the seasons, all by itself. Right now it is autumn: a warm golden glow on Home with a few leaves drifting down, an amber light around your cell and in its home, and a soft golden haze in the 3D bloodstream. It works in light and dark mode and changes with the date, no setting needed. New: ride along with your cell. On Today, tap Your inside, pick a place, and your cell travels through the vessels in the 3D world. Drag to look around while it moves, pinch to zoom, and tap Gyro to look around by tilting your phone. The more you eat low-spike and earn XP, the clearer and brighter your inside gets. Friends tree: tap a friend and send them care right from there. Your body world grew: open the 3D world on Home and tap a place. You travel through a blood vessel into seven regions of your body (brain, lungs, heart, liver, pancreas, gut, muscles) and can look around in each one by dragging, pinching or tilting your phone. Back takes you to the bloodstream. New: body journeys. On Home, tap the adventure bar and pick a ticket: your cell travels to the gut, liver, heart, brain and more, and comes back with a real fact about that place. Up to 3 trips a day, and each one lands in your adventure log. The weather on Today now opens on top even while an update note is showing. New here? You now start by planting and naming your herb, and it greets you by name. A few quick questions build your starter plan: small daily steps, each with a "Why?" and a tap straight to the right screen. You'll find it on Today, and you can redo it any time under Profile > About you. New: your cell has a home. Open your herb, then Wardrobe, and tap Home to decorate it with the pieces you own. In Community, the tree icon next to the title opens your friends tree: real friends only, by invite link or from the Community, and it only shows names, cell names and levels, never health data. Tap the weather on Today: your weather opens inside the app, with the next hours, high and low, and how today's weather affects your body and blood sugar. The black bar at the top of the profile pages is gone. New: your body world in real 3D. On Home, tap the 3D window to open it full screen. Drag to look around, pinch to zoom, and on a phone tap Use motion once, then tilt it to look around like VR. Tap a glowing place to fly there. Your herb is now a living cell. Look inside: it mirrors what you log. After a Move everything pumps, a sweet spike fills its world with sugar crystals for a few hours, water and low-spike meals keep it clear, and late at night it is awake but tired. Open it from Home and tap how you feel. A picture of your entries, not a measurement. New in your body universe: open your herb and tap the cell icon at the top. The microbe collection has 18 body buddies, from the insulin messenger to the mitochondrion, each with a real fact. You find them with meals, water, Move, scans and fasting, and repeating unlocks new colours. Under Friends you can send real friends a hug, a good night or a "drink water", and the adventure log keeps what your cell discovers on body journeys. Deep analyze, which opens your custom GPT, sits at the bottom of the scanner. Barcode, Snap food, Log meal and Water +1 all live in Scan now. Tap the herb on Home and you get just your herb: play, wardrobe, collection and its path. You can now support LOWiSPIKE on Ko-fi, right from the app: Wardrobe, Shop, Pay what you want. One-time or monthly, or simply 0 €. It's voluntary and unlocks nothing, everything stays free. New on Today: a short good-morning card once a day with your day count and one goal. Tap the Goal chip in your log to pick a rhythm, like 3 days this week or a kind streak where a missed day only pauses. In Safari, Add to Home Screen is now three illustrated steps. Tap your level: the herb path shows the next form, the rule and how much is left. Plus special quests with hints, up to 2 weekly missions, your own goals with a direct link, and your food collection. Rewards now wait for Claim. Your day has a sun now: every meal, scan, glass of water and Move fills it, and your herb cheers you on. Fill it and your herb goes out to the garden and brings you back a find. Your herb has a shop now. Open the wardrobe and tap Shop: Kometa brings one free piece every day, a new shelf three times a day, and the Mist Moon drop with three autumn pieces. Every piece shows how to earn it, XP is never spent, and nothing is for sale.

Mistys Abenteuer mit Timer erkundet jetzt wie der Autopilot, und wie weit sie kommt, hängt von ihrem Level ab. Level 1 und 2: ihre Heimatwelt, sie besucht jede Tür. Level 3: Sie fliegt auch in die Zellwelten. Level 4: Sie bricht aus und schwebt durch den äußeren Himmel der Geisterwelt. Level 5: Sie geht in deren Blasen hinein. Level 6: Sie lässt sich allein von den Strömungen von Blase zu Blase tragen. Der Autopilot (dreimal schnell auf den Controller tippen) ist eine eigene Wahl und fliegt immer überall hin, egal welches Level. Ihre Misty-Karte zeigt, was freigeschaltet ist, und das Reise-Fenster sagt, wie weit diese Reise geht.

Du kannst Misty jetzt jederzeit von ihrer Erkundung zurückrufen. Solange sie unterwegs ist, steht im Timer in ihrer leeren Bubble „Tippen zum Zurückrufen“: Ein Tipp, und sie fliegt direkt heim in ihre Bubble, bringt ihren Fund mit, und du hast sie wieder am Controller. Den gleichen Knopf gibt es im Sonnen-Fenster. Ihr nächster Ausflug ist morgen, und die Welt behält das Leuchten, das sie ihr bis dahin gegeben hat.

Kein Zwischenstück mehr, wenn Misty eine Welt verlässt. Aus einer Zellwelt und aus der Hauptwelt geht es direkt von innen nach außen: Eben ist sie noch in der Welt, im nächsten Moment draußen neben ihrer Blase, während das Innere sanft ausblendet. Die Lichtstreifen, die große leuchtende Scheibe mit Ring, der flache Farbbildschirm und die lila Fläche sind weg. Der flache blaue Bildschirm hatte eine echte Ursache: Wenn die Kamera zurückzog, wurde aus Versehen die ganze lebende Welt ausgeblendet. Das ist behoben, die Welt bleibt jetzt auf dem Bildschirm.

Wenn du vorwärts hältst, ist vor Misty kein dauerhaftes Licht mehr. Stattdessen drückt sie gegen ihre eigene dehnbare Bubble-Haut, genau wie beim Rauskommen aus ihrer ersten Bubble: Die Haut dehnt sich vor ihr in Flugrichtung, beim Losfliegen ein bisschen weiter, und wackelt zurück, wenn du loslässt. Sie neigt sich mit dem Controller, so siehst du weiter, wohin sie fliegt, und beim Rückwärtsfliegen dehnt sie sich hinter ihr. Das Schießen bleibt genau wie vorher (Controller halten und mit einem zweiten Finger doppelt tippen) und geht jetzt durch ihre Haut hindurch.

Jedes Fenster öffnet sich jetzt wie Bewegung. Tippst du auf Fasten, Essen, das Wetter, Heute oder den Klang-Knopf, wächst das Fenster aus der Stelle, die du berührt hast, wie eine kleine Blase, die sich aufdehnt, und schrumpft beim Schließen wieder dorthin zurück. Es schwebt als eine von Mistys durchsichtigen Blasen, und die Welt bleibt dahinter sichtbar. Die schnellen Auswahlen sind runde Blasen, die nacheinander aufploppen, wie Schnell bis Episch bei Bewegung: die Zeiten bei Fasten beenden, Essen fotografieren und Produkt scannen und die Wetterwerte. Der Hauptknopf leuchtet mintgrün wie eine gefüllte Bewegung-Blase. Drinnen funktioniert alles wie vorher.

Draußen in der Geisterwelt fliegt Misty jetzt auch in die Blase einer anderen Welt, wenn du den Controller ruhig gedrückt hältst (vorwärts), genau wie beim Hineinsteuern mit dem Stick. Vorher zählte nur der Stick, deshalb prallte das Vorwärtshalten an jeder Blase ab und rutschte an ihr entlang. Ein gleichmäßiges Drücken kommt jetzt auch durch, wenn die Hülle sie ein wenig zurückschubst.

Wenn du die Welt berührst, kommen die Menüs nicht mehr zurück, während Misty fliegt. Mit Autopilot oder beim Steuern kannst du die Welt drehen, festhalten oder mit zwei Fingern zoomen, und die freie Sicht bleibt: keine Felder, keine Menüleiste. Nur ein kurzes, ruhiges Tippen auf Homes eigene Welt holt alles zurück, und dieses Tippen macht sonst nichts. Draußen in der Geisterwelt holt ein Tippen die Felder nie zurück: mit Autopilot kommt nur der Controller wieder, damit du übernehmen kannst.

Misty bleibt beschäftigt, wenn sie im Autopilot aus einer Welt fliegt. Beim Rausfliegen schaut sie, wohin sie fliegt, statt sich umzudrehen und dich anzustarren, und draußen fliegt sie direkt zum nächsten Ziel, statt zu treiben und zu warten. Wenn sie sich weit draußen verirrt, schwimmt sie kleine Schleifen, statt nur dazuhängen. Hast du in einer Welt getippt, springen beim Verlassen nicht mehr überraschend alle Menüs von Home auf. Nur der Controller, den du zurückgeholt hast, bleibt, und ein Tipp auf Home bringt den Rest.

Weit hinausfliegen bringt Misty nicht mehr zurück in ihre Blase. Hältst du weiter in eine Richtung, über das tiefe Dunkel hinaus, kommt sie jetzt neben deinem Zuhause herum und fliegt weiter in neuen Raum, statt geradewegs zurück in ihre Blase. Lässt du den Stick los, um dich umzusehen, zählt das nicht mehr als Nichtstun, sie bleibt also draußen, während du schaust. Ein Wischen vom Bildschirmrand dreht beim Fliegen jetzt die Ansicht, statt die Seite zu wechseln. Und kurz die App wechseln oder wenn das Handy kurz die 3D-Grafik wegnimmt, hält sie jetzt nur an, wo sie ist, statt neu anzufangen.

Jetzt leuchtet im Dunkel der Zell-Begleiter, nicht mehr Misty. Tief in der dunklen Zone einer Welt leuchtet der kleine Begleiter neben Misty alle 3 Sekunden für einen Augenblick auf, mit einem sanften Licht, das nur zeigt, was direkt um euch beide ist. Misty selbst bleibt dunkel. Das schwache warme Leuchten der Welt, aus der ihr kommt, ist weiter da, und das Dunkel bleibt fast schwarz.

Mit Autopilot zeigt das Drehen der Welt Misty jetzt von einer neuen Seite. In einer Welt bleibt ihr Weg dort, wo er in der Welt ist: Drehst du die Welt, siehst du ihre Seite, ihr Gesicht oder ihren Rücken aus deinem neuen Blickwinkel, statt immer dieselbe Seite. Dreht dein Wischen ihr Ziel aus dem Bild, sucht sie sich ein neues im Bild. Und wenn sie eine Weile von dir weggeflogen ist, schaut sie jetzt kurz über die Schulter zu dir zurück und fliegt dann weiter. Wenn du sie selbst steuerst, ändert sich nichts.

Mit Autopilot in einer Welt blendet sich der Controller jetzt ganz aus, zusammen mit seiner kleinen Moduszeile, sodass nur Misty und die Welt bleiben. Wenn du sie selbst steuerst, bleibt er da, und ein Tippen holt ihn weiterhin zurück, damit du übernehmen kannst.

Im Dunkel verloren? Halte Ausschau nach Zuhause. Wenn du Misty weit in die dunkle Zone einer Welt fliegst, leuchtet die Welt, aus der ihr kommt, jetzt ganz schwach dort, wo sie wirklich ist, in einem matten warmen Licht. Auch wenn sie außerhalb des Bildschirms liegt, ist die Seite zu ihr hin eine Spur weniger schwarz. Das ist nur ein Hinweis, kein Pfeil: Das Dunkel bleibt fast schwarz, der Begleiter leuchtet weiter alle 3 Sekunden auf, und den Weg zurück musst du immer noch selbst finden.

In einer Welt bist jetzt nur noch du mit Misty und der Welt. Menü, Seitenleiste, Begrüßung, Wetter, Daily Quest, Heute und die Knöpfe tauchen dort nicht mehr auf, auch nicht, wenn du tippst. Misty, ihr Begleiter und der Controller bleiben, und der Weltkarte-Knopf bringt dich weiterhin zurück. Außerhalb der Welten behält alles den weichen Wasser-Look von Home statt der alten flachen Kästen.

Die Schwarzen Löcher sind weg. Nichts zieht Misty mehr hinein oder hält sie fest. Wo die Wolkenwand um eine Welt ihre dunklen Lücken hat, öffnet sich die Welt jetzt ins Dunkel, und dort kannst du immer hineinfliegen. Je tiefer du fliegst, desto dunkler wird alles, bis du und Misty kaum noch etwas seht, als wärt ihr aus dem Spiel hinausgeflogen. Alle 3 Sekunden leuchtet ihr Zell-Begleiter für einen Augenblick auf, damit du weißt, dass ihr noch da seid und nichts hängt. Steuere zurück und das Licht kommt wieder. Das Dunkel ist nie ein Ausgang. Das ist nur die Wolkenwand: Drück hinein und ihre dünne gläserne Blasenhaut wölbt sich um Misty nach außen, wie der Rand von Zuhause, wenn sie in die Geisterwelt fliegt.

Misty starrt dich nicht mehr die ganze Zeit an. Draußen in der Welt dreht sie ihren ganzen runden Körper und schaut dorthin, wohin sie fliegt: Fliegt sie seitlich, siehst du ihr Gesicht im Profil, fliegt sie weg, siehst du ihren Rücken, fliegt sie nach oben, wandert ihr Gesicht nach oben. Wenn du steuerst, schaut sie dorthin, wohin du sie gedreht hast, und beim Rückwärtsfliegen schaut sie weiter nach vorn. Mit Autopilot und wenn sie eine Welt umkreist, bevor sie hineinfliegt, schaut sie entlang ihres Wegs. Wenn sie ruht, schaut sie sich selbst um und blickt nur ab und zu zu dir zurück. Ihre Drehungen sind sanft, nie ruckartig.

Misty begegnet jetzt den Blutkörperchen, die um sie herum schweben. Draußen im Blutstrom bei Home kann ein Blutkörperchen wirklich an sie stoßen, nur wenn es tatsächlich auf ihrer Tiefe ist, nicht wenn es nur vor oder hinter ihr vorbeizieht. Sie wird ein bisschen weggeschubst, das Blutkörperchen trudelt auf eine neue Bahn, und ihr wird lustig schwindelig: Sie kippt zur Seite, schwankt kurz benommen, fängt sich und richtet sich wieder auf.
